milestone: M3: Training data model, week-1 baseline program generation and program management. There are 50 small PRs in 11 tracks. Domain contracts come first (vocabulary, plan contract, metrics, wording, catalogue). Then come the serial schema chain (6 migration slots), program services, the logged-training write and read paths, and the pure generator, whose full stage list exists from its first slice so stage slices never share a file. Screens come last: Train and session detail, the edit sheets, History, and Today's Build moment and plan. One journey proves the whole flow end to end, and docs close the milestone. This revision fixes all 27 problems the critic raised. It was re-checked against origin/m2/11-profile-services, origin/main f489491 (which now includes withCommitted, #27), fix/m2-section-saves-serialize (lockSection) and wip/m2-onboarding-ui (ChoiceGroup, ExercisesEditor, the private form helpers).

VERSIONING (ADR 0010, written in m3/07): copy-on-write at week granularity, with membership tables.
- A version's tree is its rows in program_version_blocks and program_version_weeks.
- An edit copies only the affected week subtrees (week → sessions → planned exercises → set prescriptions, run segments and details). The copies get new row ids and keep their lineage_id. Every other membership row is reused.
- programs.current_version_id is the only mutable pointer. It moves forward by compare-and-set inside the revising transaction (SELECT … FOR UPDATE), so a stale base gives ProgramConflictError, never a lost update.
- Screens address sessions by lineage_id (/train/session/<lineage>, with ?v=n for an older version), so URLs survive edits.
- Rejected: per-row validity ranges (UPDATEs on history and range predicates in every read); a full deep copy per version; mutable rows plus an audit log; event sourcing.

IMMUTABILITY IS ENFORCED BY POSTGRES. TRUNCATE IS THE ONLY BYPASS.
- plpgsql guards live in custom migrations (drizzle-kit generate --custom), never appended to generated files.
- Planned tables, programming decisions and training_audit refuse UPDATE.
- On program heads, only current_version_id (forward, to the program's own version), status and archived_at may change.
- Logged tables allow UPDATE for owner edits, and every UPDATE that changes content is audited.
- DELETE is refused on every history and logged table, always, with no session flag. Owners delete logged rows softly (deleted_at).
- TRUNCATE fires no row triggers, so it is the one bypass. Only test and reset code uses it: M2's withCommitted, the e2e resetPrograms and the explain database reset. M3 adds no BEFORE TRUNCATE guard, because withCommitted relies on TRUNCATE.
- Every M3 table with rows owned by someone reaches owners through FKs (ownerRef, or a parent that has one), training_audit included. withCommitted's `truncate owners … cascade` therefore clears it. exercises is the one deliberate exception (see the library decision).
- scripts/history-guards.test.ts fails if server code contains `truncate`, `session_replication_role` or `disable trigger`. Server code means src/lib/server, +server.ts, +page.server.ts, +layout.server.ts and hooks.
- History rows reference mutable profile rows (goals, commitments) by uuid with no FK, as M2's training_goal_events does. SET NULL or CASCADE can then never trip a guard.
- Consequence: deleting the owner row is refused, because its CASCADE reaches guarded tables. auth:reset-owner keeps the owner row, and docs/security.md says so (m3/48).

CHECKS COVER CLOSED VOCABULARIES ONLY, following M2's convention, so a new value never forces a migration outside the serial chain.

Numeric ranges and coherence rules are CHECKed too.
- Not CHECKed (open vocabularies that M3–M7 extend): decision kind, rule key, phase, week kind, session type, set role, run segment kind, other-session kind, substitution reason, movement pattern, muscles and tags. Services validate them with the domain types and zod, and the seed validates them through parseTable.
- m3/01 lists every M3 decision kind up front, including default_assumed (a 'not told yet' default) and goal_excluded (a paused goal).
- SUBSTITUTION_REASONS already includes M4's reasons: situational, equipment_unavailable, dislike, pain, injury, coach_suggestion and owner_choice.
- TypeScript forces every emitted decision kind into the list, and m3/28 also checks it at runtime.

STATUS. Planned, skipped and moved are stored on each version's immutable session rows. Skip and move are owner edits, so each creates a version. 'Completed' is derived in program reads (m3/25) from completed workouts matched by planned_lineage_id. Logging training (M4) therefore never creates a version, and a completed session stays completed in later versions; m3/29 proves this.

EXERCISE LIBRARY AS DOMAIN DATA.
- Each exercise is one line of a validated pipe table in a template literal.
- Every table starts with the fixed header `key | name | aliases | pattern | primary | secondary | equipment | group | skill | reps | seconds | uni | measure/load | tags | disciplines | lift`:
  - seconds holds the default seconds of a time-measured entry, or '-'
  - uni is 'y' for unilateral entries, or '-'
  - parseTable requires the header, and check-budgets uses it as the catalogue's bundle signature
- Prettier does not reflow these lines, so about 160 entries stay reviewable. defineExercise objects would come to about 1,800 lines.
- The tables live in src/lib/domain/exercises/catalogue/{lower,upper}.ts. The two parts are written in parallel, in separate files with separate substitution groups; m3/06 merges after m3/05.
- `exercises` holds catalogue rows (a key, no owner) and custom rows (an owner_id, no key).
- owner_id has NO FK to owners. withCommitted truncates owners with CASCADE, and an FK would empty the whole library in the middle of the integration suite. Every query scopes custom rows to their owner, and the owner is never deleted.
- runMigrations seeds the library after migrating, under the same advisory lock, with one jsonb_to_recordset upsert keyed by key:
  - changed rows are updated
  - removed keys are retired, never deleted
  - a key that reappears is un-retired
  Preview deployments share one Neon branch, so PRs with different catalogues retire and restore keys in turn. This is expected and harmless, and docs/deployment.md says so.
- The seed uses raw SQL and imports only domain modules, with explicit .ts specifiers. scripts/catalogue-node.test.ts runs migrate.ts under plain Node, and CI's pnpm db:migrate runs the seed.
- The generator reads the catalogue from code (CATALOGUE), never from database rows, and refers to exercises by key (custom ones as custom:<uuid>). Keys resolve to ids at store time, retired rows included, so a preview re-seeded by another PR cannot change or break a build.

TRAINING LOG.
- One `workouts` parent row per logged session, kind strength | run | other. It holds the device idempotency id (client_id UNIQUE), planned_session_id and planned_lineage_id, start and finish times, duration and session RPE.
- Detail rows are 1:1: run_records with run_record_segments, and other_session_records with a CHECKed jsonb metrics array.
- set_records carries a UNIQUE client_mutation_id, the weight as entered plus a generated exact weight_kg, and an e1rm_kg stored at write time. editSet recomputes e1rm_kg whenever weight, unit, reps, RPE or the warm-up or skipped flags change.
- Every logged table and training_audit carries owner_id (ownerRef):
  - withCommitted's truncate clears them
  - the audit trigger reads the owner generically from the row
  - M9's export is owner-scoped
  - integration tests filter audit rows by row_id
- Replay contract, frozen in m3/30 and documented in m3/48 for M4's outbox:
  - Creates (workout, set, segment, run, other session, recovery note, substitution) carry a device id and use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then return the stored row with duplicate: true. A replay with a different payload never overwrites: the stored row wins, and the result reports matches: false so M4 can tell the owner.
  - Edits send absolute values keyed by row id, so they are idempotent by value. A replayed edit that changes nothing does not bump updated_at and writes no audit row. M4's outbox applies one row's mutations in order, so edits need no mutation id of their own.
  - Deletes are soft. A replayed delete returns the already-deleted row unchanged and writes no audit row.
- Triggers:
  - BEFORE UPDATE bumps updated_at, but only when the content changed
  - AFTER UPDATE writes before and after JSON, with the actor and owner, to training_audit, only when the content changed
  - BEFORE DELETE always refuses
  - training_audit itself refuses UPDATE and DELETE
- Situational substitutions are stored only on the session: planned_exercises.substituted_from_exercise_id (M3) and workout_substitutions (M4). Neither ever writes exercise_preferences.

HISTORY QUERIES ARE DEFINED ONCE.
- Every builder lives in src/lib/server/db/queries/{history,programs}.ts. Repositories run them, and db:explain explains the same builders.
- Planned-session builders live in queries/programs.ts (m3/20, m3/25, m3/29). sessionsInRange in queries/history.ts composes m3/25's plannedSessionsInRange with the workouts query; it never redefines it.
- pnpm db:explain is a Vitest project ('explain'), because plain Node cannot load the app's imports. It:
  - resets coach_explain, migrates and seeds it
  - loads a deterministic two-year dataset
  - prints EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for every builder to stdout and to test-results/explain.md
  - runs in CI
- The gate is defined by size, not by table name. After ANALYZE, a relation is large when reltuples ≥ 5,000 or relpages ≥ 50.
  - Every builder declares its expected index. On a large relation the plan must use that index and must not Seq Scan.
  - Small relations (workouts at about 600 rows, exercises at about 200, programs, decisions) may Seq Scan, which is the right plan at single-owner scale. Their plans are recorded but not gated.
- PRs and best e1RM across all exercises drive a LATERAL from the small exercises table (catalogue rows, retired ones included, plus the owner's custom rows). Each exercise probes the (owner_id, exercise_id, e1rm_kg desc) and rep-max indexes, never a DISTINCT over set_records.
- Version history is keyset-paginated, 20 per page.
- db:explain is the last slot of the serial schema chain, so any index fix is a migration in order.
- Aggregations are index range scans followed by the pure domain metrics, so 'hard set' has a single definition.

GENERATOR.
- Pure domain code lives in src/lib/domain/programming/:
  - input normalisation with explicit defaults, a fingerprint (FNV-1a over canonical JSON) and a seeded PRNG (mulberry32), with no clock and no Math.random; startsOn and firstPlannedDay are inputs
  - numeric rules in one file per area, rules/<area>.ts
  - a decision builder with a template for every kind
  - one module per stage
- THE STAGE LIST EXISTS FROM m3/13. generate.ts runs: demand → blocks → commitments → strength → running → other → placement → volume → loads → progression → timefit.
  - m3/13 creates every stage file in stages/ as an identity stub.
  - Each later slice replaces only its own stub: m3/17 strength and timefit; m3/18 commitments, running and other; m3/21 loads and progression; m3/22 volume; m3/23 placement.
  - Only m3/28 edits generate.ts afterwards, adding output validation and the purpose decision.
- FINGERPRINT = canonical input + a catalogue digest (computed in the domain over CATALOGUE's content and the owner's custom exercises) + GENERATOR_ID. The canonical input excludes timestamps, row ids, start dates and the profile time zone, so recording the device zone at build never turns a retry into a conflict.
- Each version stores its input snapshot, digest, generator id, startsOn and firstPlannedDay. Reproduction is guaranteed for the same digest and generator id, and a test proves it.
- Preview → build regenerates and compares, so no drafts are stored. ProgrammingConflictError carries reason 'profile', 'library' or 'start_date', each with its own designed copy.
- Building is idempotent against a double tap. The source is owner or coach, so M5 calls the same functions as tools.
- M1's maths is reused, never redefined:
  - sessionLoad (session load)
  - estimateOneRepMax (set e1RM)
  - loadForTarget and percentOfOneRepMax (week-1 and progression loads)
  - roundToIncrement with DEFAULT_LOAD_INCREMENT (plate rounding)
  - formatDuration, formatWeight, paceSecondsPer and convertPace (wording)
  - toMetres and fromMetres (distances)

'NOT TOLD YET' DEFAULTS. A complete M2 profile may hold only one goal and daysPerWeek. m3/10 applies every default in rules/defaults.ts and lists it on the input as an assumption. m3/13 turns each assumption into a default_assumed decision with a 'why' that points to the Profile section.
- availableDays empty → any day of the week.
- preferredTimes empty → no time of day. 'varies' gives no time of day and is never a second distinct time.
- sessionMinutes null → 60, M2's suggested value.
- Equipment not set → M2's 'commercial' gym preset (open question).
- A commitment with intensity null → moderate. Duration null → the discipline's default in rules/defaults.ts (60 min; 90 for Muay Thai).
- No running specifics with a running goal → week 1 is time-based (easy runs of 30 min at RPE 4–5, a 45-minute long run, no quality session).
- No Muay Thai specifics and no commitment → technical sessions of sessionMinutes at RPE 6.
- Paused goals are excluded from shaping, with a goal_excluded decision. If every open goal is paused, their disciplines are planned at maintenance.
- A custom-discipline goal gets its commitments. Without one, it gets 'other' sessions in its allocated slots, titled with its name, at RPE 6 for sessionMinutes, with a decision saying its content is the owner's own.
- m3/13 adds a 'minimal' scenario (one goal and daysPerWeek only), asserted in m3/28 and in m3/36's integration test.

SESSION LENGTH.
- sessionMinutes limits every generated session: strength, easy and quality runs, mobility and S&C.
- The long run follows the running rules and may exceed it, with a time_trimmed or priority_tradeoff decision saying so (open question).
- Commitments keep their own stated or default duration.
- timefit is the LAST stage, so sets added by volume (m3/22) and progression (m3/21) are re-checked every week. Trimming order: accessories, then back-off sets, never the top set. Each trim writes a time_trimmed decision.
- When a goal's hard-set range cannot fit, volume adds sets only while the estimate fits and records a priority_tradeoff decision.
- m3/28 asserts that every generated non-long-run session in every week is estimated at or under sessionMinutes.

ONE DAY RULE, in m3/13's demand.ts. Strength (m3/17), running and commitments (m3/18) and placement (m3/23) all use it.
- daysPerWeek counts every training day, commitment days included.
- Training days = min(daysPerWeek, |available ∪ commitment days|), with availability defaulted as above.
- Free days = max(0, training days − commitment days). When commitments fill the stated days, a day_allocation decision says that no extra day is added.
- A commitment counts toward its discipline's quota:
  - running and distance_running → runs and weekly run volume, by duration
  - powerlifting, weightlifting, strength and hypertrophy → strength days, with no hard sets credited, because the class sets the content
  - muay_thai, athletic and custom → other sessions
- Free days go to disciplines by goal priority.
- A second session in a day, including a session added on a commitment day, is allowed only when the preferred times hold two distinct times ('varies' excluded) and the session length allows it. Otherwise the lowest-priority session is dropped, with a decision.
- SEVERAL DATED EVENTS: the highest-priority dated goal shapes the block structure and its outline phases. Another event inside the first block gets a taper week, with a decision naming it. One beyond the first block becomes a note on the outline.

INTERFERENCE RULES ARE ONE PURE MODULE (m3/09). Placement uses it to build the week, and the move edit uses it to warn. A move that breaks a rule is allowed, but the warning is returned and written into the decision's 'why'. demandOf also classifies commitment sessions by discipline and intensity: a hard strength class counts as very demanding. M7 extends the table.

THE OWNER'S LOCAL DATE.
- It is localDay(instant, the profile's IANA time zone), from fix/m2-body-weight-local-day.
- Services take explicit dates. src/lib/server/local-date.ts (ownerToday) is created in m3/27, the first slice that needs it (the fixture route); every route uses it from then on.
- M2 builds no UI for the time zone, so it starts at 'UTC'.
- The Build preview and build actions both carry the device's time zone, read with Intl at submit time and never during hydration. Both compute today from that same zone, so they always agree.
- Build records the zone through the M2 profile service when it differs. From then on, Train and Today use it. The fingerprint ignores the zone, so a retried build still returns the same program.
- startsOn and firstPlannedDay are returned by the preview and sent back with build. Build keeps them while firstPlannedDay ≥ today. After a midnight rollover it returns the start_date conflict ('It's a new day'), never 'your profile changed'.
- Rejected: a tzo cookie. It is offset-based, needs an app.html script and a CSP hash change, and would be a second source of truth.

E2E AND INTEGRATION DATA.

No guard is involved. A test asserts that every table outside M1/M2 except exercises is empty afterwards, so a later table cannot be missed.

First block: the default is 1 baseline week + 3 accumulation weeks + a deload, shortened to a build and taper when the highest-priority event is under 6 weeks away. Confirm, or do you prefer 4 weeks?

Several dated events: the highest-priority dated goal shapes the block. Another event inside the first block gets a taper week; one beyond it is only noted on the outline. Is that the owner's intent for a fight plus a marathon?

Days per week: daysPerWeek counts commitment days, so 5 days with Muay Thai Tue/Thu leaves 3 free days. When commitments fill the stated days, no extra day is added. - empty available days → any day
- no session length → 60 min
- equipment not set → M2's commercial-gym preset
- commitment intensity → moderate; duration → 60 min (90 for Muay Thai)
- no running specifics → a time-based week 1
- paused goals → excluded (maintenance if all are paused)
Each default is shown as a decision. Is the commercial-gym default right, or should unset equipment mean bodyweight only?

Commitments by discipline: a running club counts as a run (and toward weekly volume by duration), and a strength or CrossFit-style class counts as a strength day with no hard sets credited, because the class sets its content. Is that right?

Session length: sessionMinutes limits every generated session except the long run, which follows the running rules and is explained when longer, and commitments, which keep their own durations. Should the long run also be capped?

Moves stay within the session's own week, only for sessions and destinations dated today or later. A move that breaks an interference rule is warned and recorded, not blocked. Are cross-week moves needed, or should any rule be a hard block?
